caseno: Appeal from Original Decree (FA) No. 18 of 1995.
lawyer:
Zakir Hossain Majumder, Advocate---For the Appellant. 
Biswojit Roy, Advocate-----For the Respondents.
parties:
Pubali Bank Ltd ----- Appellant
vs
Md Nurul Hoque and  another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Arayesuddin J: This appeal, at the instance of the plaintiff Pubali Bank, has been preferred against the judgment and preliminary decree, dated 21-9-1994, passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Manikganj, in Artha Rin Case No. 1 of 1994, decreeing the suit in preliminary form. 

 2. Fact necessary to dispose of the appeal, in brief, is that respondents took loan for running business of rod and cement. Loan of Taka 1,75,201 was sanctioned in their name in the year 1990 as per sanction letter No. HO/4AD/ PROP/1140/90. Subsequently, this amount was raised to Taka 2,00,000. The period of re-payment of loan was 31st July, 1991. Respondents admitting all the terms of the sanction letter withdrew the amount by mortgaging their land in favour of the appellant-Bank. But the respondents did not pay the loan amount. As a result notice was issued to them on 26-12-1992. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were requested several times to pay the loan amount. On examining the CC account of defendant No. 1 it is found that till 9-3-1994 the unpaid amount was at Taka 3,70,617 of which Taka 1,77,200 is the principal amount and Taka 1,51,580 is the simple interest and the penal interest is Taka 87,942. The respondents have not paid those amounts. So, the plaintiff-Bank instituted the aforementioned suit which has been decreed on contest by the impugned judgment and decree. 

 3. On behalf of the appellant-Bank, the learned Counsel Mr Zakir Hossain Majumder, submitted that the learned Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit in preliminary form and assessed the interest at the rate of Taka 10% only which is not sustainable in the eye of law in view of section 8 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. He submitted that respondents are defaulters and it has been established by the evidences that the plaintiff-Bank has obtained the decree of Taka 2,56,933 upto the period of 9-3-1994. But the learned Court has awarded interest at the rate of Taka 10% for the period from the institution of the suit till the realisation of the decretal amount and if the decretal amount is not realised, then the plaintiff-Bank is entitled to realise the decretal amount by selling the mortgaged property. He submitted that this assessment of interest is against the principle of section 8 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. He further submitted that the Court by exercising his discretion exempted the respondents from paying 50% of the interest of the loan money. So, he submitted that the Bank could not be punished twice, one by exempting 50% interest and another by reducing the interest as mentioned in the sanction letter. 

 5. We have perused the impugned judgment and the preliminary decree. Till now claim of the decree has not been satisfied. Now the question is, whether the rate of interest assessed by the Court is proper or not. At the end of the impugned judgment it is found that the Court has exercised his discretion and exempted the judgment-debtor-respondents from paying 50% of the interest assessed on the claim. But he has assessed only 10% interest during the pendency of the suit and till the realisation of the decretal amount. The learned trial Court gave emphasis on the statement of the local manager of the plaintiff-Bank. But the Bank is a financial institution. It deals with the public money. Particular official has got no personal option to deal in the financial matter. Therefore, the statement of the local manager of the plaintiff-Bank in his cross-examination is not binding upon the Bank. The learned trial Court considered the claim of the Bank and exempted 50% interest. So, he cannot reduce the rate of interest which is in the sanction letter. In view of that we find merit in the appeal. 

 6. In the result, the appeal is allowed on contest without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and preliminary decree is modified by assessing the interest at the rate of 18% which is in the sanction letter. With this modification the impugned judgment and the preliminary decree of the trial Court is hereby affirmed.
